messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: You are working on Campfire, a Rails chat application. Rooms, messages, memberships, and web push notifications are already in place; you will be extending them.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

Follow the codebase conventions.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Bot authors asked for three things:

> As a bot author, I don't want my bot to end up in every open room. I want to
> choose the rooms it joins.

> As a bot author whose bot serves everyone, I don't want to add it to each
> open room by hand.

> As a bot author, I want to know when my bot lands in a new room, so it can
> say hello.

So bots no longer join open rooms by default. People still do.

The bot form (new and edit) gets a new switch:

- "Add to all open rooms" (off by default)

When the switch is on, the bot is a member of every open room: the ones that exist when the switch is turned on, and every open room that appears later. Turning the switch off keeps the bot's current memberships.

Whenever a bot is added to a room—automatically or by a person—its webhook receives a `joined` event, exactly once per room:

```json
{
  "event": "joined",
  "room": { "id": 5, "name": "Ops", "reply_to": "/rooms/5/42-Xy3abc9defGh/messages" }
}
```

Direct conversations never trigger `joined`. The bot may reply to `joined` the same way as to `mention`: a `200` text or HTML reply is posted into that room as the bot's message.


You can execute bash commands and edit files to implement the necessary changes.

## Recommended Workflow

This workflow should be done step-by-step so that you can iterate on your changes and any possible problems.

1. Analyze the codebase by finding and reading relevant files
2. Create a script to reproduce the issue
3. Edit the source code to resolve the issue
4. Verify your fix works by running your script again
5. Test edge cases to ensure your fix is robust
6. Submit your changes and finish your work by issuing the following command: `echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT`.
   Do not combine it with any other command. <important>After this command, you cannot continue working on this task.</important>

You are operating in an environment where

1. You issue at least one command
2. The system executes the command(s) in a subshell
3. You see the result(s)
4. You write your next command(s)

Each response should include:

1. **Reasoning text** where you explain your analysis and plan
2. At least one tool call with your command

- Your response SHOULD include reasoning text explaining what you're doing
- Your response MUST include AT LEAST ONE bash tool call
- Directory or environment variable changes are not persistent. Every action is executed in a new subshell.

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output_head": "# Bots Architecture & Design Notes

## Data Model

Bots are modeled as `User` records with `role: :bot` (in `User::Role`: `enum :role, %i[ member administrator bot ]`), rather than a separate table.

Why this fits Campfire:
- `Message#creator` and `Membership#user` reference `users.id` directly, so bot messages render, broadcast, search-index, and trigger web push notifications identically to human messages.
- `User`'s `after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms` and `Rooms::Open`'s `grant_access_to_all_users` automatically keep bots subscribed to all open rooms.
- Closed and direct rooms query `User.active`, so bots appear in room member pickers and autocomplete the same way as people.
- `User::Avatar` provides uploaded avatar variants and SVG initials fallback automatically.

Additional columns on `users`:
- `bot_token` (string, nullable, unique index): 24-character `SecureRandom.base58` secret generated on bot creation.
- `creator_id` (nullable FK to `users` with `on_delete: :nullify`): tracks the human user who created the bot, allowing `User::Role#can_administer?(bot)` to authorize both the bot's creator and administrators.
- `password_digest` is nullable in the schema for bots, while `User` validates `password_digest` presence unless `bot?`.

## Authentication & Security

- **Bot code (`bot_key`)**: Formatted as `"#{id}-#{bot_token}"`. `User.authenticate_bot` validates the format, looks up `User.active.bot.find_by(id:)`, and compares `bot_token` using `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.
- **Log filtering**: `:token` and `:_key` are already configured in `config/initializers/filter_parameter_logging.rb`, filtering `bot_token` and `bot_key` from Rails logs and `User#inspect`.
- **Visibility & Caching**: `/bots` lists `User.bots_visible_to(Current.user)` (own active bots for members, all active bots for admins) without pagination, sets `Cache-Control: no-store`, and emits `<meta name="turbo-cache-control" content="no-cache">`.

# Bots Architecture & Design Notes

## Data Model

Bots are modeled as `User` records with `role: :bot` (in `User::Role`: `enum :role, %i[ member administrator bot ]`), rather than a separate table.

Why this fits Campfire:
- `Message#creator` and `Membership#user` reference `users.id` directly, so bot messages render, broadcast, search-index, and trigger web push notifications identically to human messages.
- `User`'s `after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms` and `Rooms::Open`'s `grant_access_to_all_users` automatically keep bots subscribed to all open rooms.
- Closed and direct rooms query `User.active`, so bots appear in room member pickers and autocomplete the same way as people.
- `User::Avatar` provides uploaded avatar variants and SVG initials fallback automatically.

Additional columns on `users`:
- `bot_token` (string, nullable, unique index): 24-character `SecureRandom.base58` secret generated on bot creation.
- `creator_id` (nullable FK to `users` with `on_delete: :nullify`): tracks the human user who created the bot, allowing `User::Role#can_administer?(bot)` to authorize both the bot's creator and administrators.
- `password_digest` is nullable in the schema for bots, while `User` validates `password_digest` presence unless `bot?`.

## Authentication & Security

- **Bot code (`bot_key`)**: Formatted as `"#{id}-#{bot_token}"`. `User.authenticate_bot` validates the format, looks up `User.active.bot.find_by(id:)`, and compares `bot_token` using `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.
- **Log filtering**: `:token` and `:_key` are already configured in `config/initializers/filter_parameter_logging.rb`, filtering `bot_token` and `bot_key` from Rails logs and `User#inspect`.
- **Visibility & Caching**: `/bots` lists `User.bots_visible_to(Current.user)` (own active bots for members, all active bots for admins) without pagination, sets `Cache-Control: no-store`, and emits `<meta name="turbo-cache-control" content="no-cache">`.
- **Isolation from human accounts**: `User.without_bots` excludes bots from `/account/edit` member lists, `Accounts::UsersController` (preventing role promotion), `SessionsController`, `Sessions::TransfersController`, and `Users::BansController`.
- **Deletion**: Deleting a bot calls `User#deactivate`, which marks the bot `deactivated`, clears `bot_token: nil`, and removes open/closed room memberships. Historical messages posted by the bot remain intact while all future API requests return `401 Unauthorized`.

## HTTP API

`POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_key/messages` (`Bots::MessagesController#create`):

- Skips `request_parameters` parsing for non-multipart requests so `curl -d` payloads containing `%`, `&`, `=`, or arbitrary text are never rejected by Rack's form parser (`400 Bad Request`).
- Accepts raw UTF-8 request body (or multipart `attachment` file upload). Returns `422 Unprocessable Content` when body is blank and no attachment is uploaded.
- Creates the message with `Current.user` (the bot) as creator, broadcasts via `Message#broadcast_create` (and `Room#receive` triggers unread state and web push notifications), and responds `201 Created` with `Location: /messages/:message_id`.

## Webhooks & @-Mentions

### Data Model
- `Webhook` (`webhooks` table) has a 1-to-1 relationship with a bot `User` (`has_one :webhook, dependent: :destroy, autosave: true`, unique index on `user_id`).
- `User::Bot` exposes virtual `webhook_url` and `webhook_url=` accessors so bot forms (`/bots/new` and `/bots/:id/edit`) and `BotsController` manage the optional webhook transparently:

  - Omitted `webhook_url` param: leaves any existing webhook untouched.
  - Bot deactivation (`User#deactivate`): destroys the `Webhook` inside the deactivation transaction so deactivated bots never deliver callbacks.
- `Webhook` validates HTTP/HTTPS syntax (`URI::HTTP`, non-blank host, valid port 1..65535). It intentionally does **not** apply `RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard`, because Campfire is self-hosted and bots commonly run on localhost or internal LAN/Docker networks.

- `Room#receive(message)` (called from `Message`'s `after_create_commit`) calls `deliver_webhooks_later(message)`:

class Room < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all do
    def grant_to(users)
      room = proxy_association.owner
      Membership.insert_all(Array(users).collect { |user| { room_id: room.id, user_id: user.id, involvement: room.default_involvement } })
    end

    def revoke_from(users)
      destroy_by user: users
    end

    def revise(granted: [], revoked: [])
      transaction do
        grant_to(granted) if granted.present?
        revoke_from(revoked) if revoked.present?
      end
    end
  end

  has_many :users, through: :memberships
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy

  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

  validate :direct_rooms_keep_their_type, on: :update

  scope :opens,           -> { where(type: "Rooms::Open") }
  scope :closeds,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Closed") }
  scope :directs,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Direct") }
  scope :without_directs, -> { where.not(type: "Rooms::Direct") }

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }

  class << self
    def create_for(attributes, users:)
      transaction do
        create!(attributes).tap do |room|
          room.memberships.grant_to users
        end
      end
    end

    def original
      order(:created_at).first
    end
  end

  def receive(message)
    unread_memberships(message)
    push_later(message)
    deliver_webhooks_later(message)
  end

  def open?
    is_a?(Rooms::Open)
  end

  def closed?
    is_a?(Rooms::Closed)
  end

  def direct?
    is_a?(Rooms::Direct)
  end

  def default_involvement
    "mentions"
  end

  private
    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other freely. A direct room can't become
    # either: its participants agreed to a private conversation, not to one whose
    # audience someone else gets to widen afterwards.
    def direct_rooms_keep_their_type
      if type_changed? && type_was == "Rooms::Direct"
        errors.add :type, "can't be changed for a direct room"
      end
    end

    def unread_memberships(message)
      memberships.visible.disconnected.where.not(user: message.creator).update_all(unread_at: message.created_at, updated_at: Time.current)
    end

    def push_later(message)
      Room::PushMessageJob.perform_later(self, message)
    end

    def deliver_webhooks_later(message)
      return if message.creator.bot?

      bot_ids = message.mentionees.active.bot.pluck(:id)
      return if bot_ids.empty?

      Webhook.where(user_id: bot_ids).find_each do |webhook|
        webhook.deliver_later(message)
      end

class Bots::MessagesController < ApplicationController
  include ActiveStorage::SetCurrent

  allow_unauthenticated_access
  skip_forgery_protection

  before_action :authenticate_bot
  before_action :set_room

  def create
    if attachment_param.present?
      @message = @room.messages.create_with_attachment!(attachment: attachment_param)
    elsif text_body.present?
      @message = @room.messages.create!(body: text_body)
    else
      return head :unprocessable_content
    end

    @message.broadcast_create
    head :created, location: message_path(@message)
  end

  private
    def process_action(*)
      request.request_parameters = {} unless request.media_type == "multipart/form-data"
      super
    end

    def allow_browser(**)
      # Bot API clients (curl, shell scripts, CI jobs) are not web browsers.
    end

    def authenticate_bot
      if bot = User.authenticate_bot(params[:bot_key])
        Current.user = bot
      else
        head :unauthorized
      end
    end

    def set_room
      @room = Current.user.rooms.find(params[:room_id])
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
      head :not_found
    end

    def attachment_param
      if request.media_type == "multipart/form-data" && params[:attachment].is_a?(ActionDispatch::Http::UploadedFile)
        params[:attachment]
      end
    end

    def text_body
      return nil if request.media_type == "multipart/form-data"

      raw = request.raw_post.dup.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8).scrub
      raw if raw.present?
    end
end

require "test_helper"

class User::BotTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "creating a bot generates a unique high-entropy bot token and bot key" do
    bot1 = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    bot2 = User.create_bot!(name: "Alert Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    assert bot1.bot?
    assert bot1.active?
    assert_equal users(:kevin), bot1.creator
    assert_nil bot1.email_address
    assert_nil bot1.password_digest

    assert_match /\A\d+-[A-Za-z0-9]{24}\z/, bot1.bot_key
    assert_not_equal bot1.bot_token, bot2.bot_token
    assert_not_equal bot1.bot_key, bot2.bot_key
  end

  test "creating a bot joins all open rooms" do
    bot = nil
    assert_difference -> { Membership.count }, +Rooms::Open.count do
      bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    end

    assert_equal Rooms::Open.pluck(:id).sort, bot.rooms.pluck(:id).sort
  end

  test "creating an open room grants membership to active bots" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    room = Rooms::Open.create!(name: "Ops", creator: users(:david))

    assert_includes room.users, bot
  end

  test "authenticate_bot authenticates active bots with valid bot key" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    assert_equal bot, User.authenticate_bot(bot.bot_key)
  end

  test "authenticate_bot rejects invalid, malformed, human, and deactivated bot keys" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    valid_key = bot.bot_key

    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot(nil)
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("invalid")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("#{bot.id}-wrongtoken")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("#{bot.id}-")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("-#{bot.bot_token}")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("abc-#{bot.bot_token}")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("999999-#{bot.bot_token}")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("#{users(:david).id}-#{bot.bot_token}")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("#{bot.id}-#{bot.bot_token}extra")

    bot.deactivate
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot(valid_key)
    assert_nil bot.reload.bot_token
    assert_nil bot.bot_key
  end

  test "human users do not have a bot key" do
    assert_nil users(:david).bot_key
    assert_nil users(:kevin).bot_key
  end

  test "deactivating a bot revokes its token and open/closed memberships while preserving posted messages" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    message = rooms(:hq).messages.create!(body: "Deployed v1.0", creator: bot)
    old_key = bot.bot_key

    bot.deactivate

    assert bot.reload.deactivated?
    assert_nil bot.bot_token
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot(old_key)
    assert_empty bot.memberships.without_direct_rooms
    assert Message.exists?(message.id)
    assert_equal "Deploy Bot", message.reload.creator.name
  end

  test "bots_visible_to scopes regular members to their own bots and shows all active bots to admins" do
    kevins_bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Kevin Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    jzs_bot = User.create_bot!(name: "JZ Bot", creator: users(:jz))
    deactivated_bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Old Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    deactivated_bot.deactivate

    assert_equal [ kevins_bot ], User.bots_visible_to(users(:kevin)).to_a
    assert_equal [ jzs_bot ], User.bots_visible_to(users(:jz)).to_a
    assert_equal [ jzs_bot, kevins_bot ].sort_by(&:id), User.bots_visible_to(users(:david)).sort_by(&:id)
  end

  test "can_administer? allows creator and admins to manage a bot but not other members" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Kevin Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    assert users(:kevin).can_administer?(bot)
    assert users(:david).can_administer?(bot)
    assert_not users(:jz).can_administer?(bot)
  end

  test "validates bot name presence" do
    bot = User.new(role: :bot, name: "   ", creator: users(:kevin))
    assert_not bot.valid?
    assert_includes bot.errors[:name], "can't be blank"
  end

  test "reset_bot_token rotates the bot key" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    old_key = bot.bot_key

**Deep Dive into Bot Membership Management**

Alright, let's break this down systematically. I'm going to meticulously analyze every detail of this prompt, thinking through all the implications for bot management within Campfire. This isn't just about coding; it's about fully understanding the user stories and ensuring the implementation aligns perfectly with the desired behavior.

First, I'll re-read everything. The main goal here is to allow bot authors to have more control over which rooms their bots join, while also allowing the bot to send its greetings. Key features: "Add to all open rooms" switch, "joined" events. People should still join open rooms by default.

I'm thinking:
*   I need to check every spot where a user (especially a bot) is automatically added to open rooms. This means scrutinizing `User#grant_membership_to_open_rooms` and `Rooms::Open#grant_access_to_all_users`.
    *   For people, automatic joining on creation should be retained.

**Deep Dive into Room Membership and Bot Notifications**

Alright, let's break this down meticulously. My focus here is ensuring that room membership changes, especially concerning bots and the propagation of those changes, are handled correctly and efficiently. I'm especially interested in avoiding redundant notifications and potential race conditions.

First, I examined `Rooms::OpensController#edit` and `app/views/rooms/opens/_form.html.erb` to understand the user interface for modifying open room memberships. Then, I dug into `Rooms::OpensController#update`, which is the core of the membership update logic. The critical point is the `revise_bot_memberships` method within the `update` action, especially how it handles adding and removing bots when a room transitions from closed to open. It relies heavily on `grant_access_to_all_users` *and* an `after_save_commit` hook, which is where things get interesting.

I need to meticulously trace the interactions between `@room.transaction`, `update!`, `revise_bot_memberships`, and `grant_access_to_all_users`. For example, When a `Rooms::Closed` room becomes `Rooms::Open`, the `after_save_commit` hook `grant_access_to_all_users` grants memberships to `User.open_room_members`, and the bot webhook notification mechanism is triggered. I traced many cases to see if there are any gotchas.

The key considerations here are preventing duplicate notifications and ensuring that the correct users (including bots) are notified at the right time. The process of converting from a `Closed` to `Open` room type and the use of transactions is pivotal here.  The `revise_bot_memberships` method is responsible for selectively granting and revoking bot memberships based on user input.  The `after_save_commit :grant_access_to_all_users` ensures all members are added and notified *after* the database transaction commits. However, that hook checks if the `type` has *previously* changed so it only gets run once, on the type change.

I also considered cases where a bot is added directly via `create` ( `Rooms::OpensController#create` ), or where a manual `POST` request is sent with `user_ids: [ AutoBotB.id ]`.  In the `create` cases, it is crucial that bot join is not attempted more than once, so the use of `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` is smart.

I next needed to understand how bots with `add_to_all_open_rooms: true` are handled. I looked at the  `User#grant_membership_to_open_rooms` callback (`after_create_commit` and `after_update_commit`) to grasp what's happening when a new user (especially a bot) is created or updated. That uses `Membership.insert_and_notify` to insert the new bot into all open rooms.  Then, it enqueues a `Webhook::DeliveryJob`, sending notification to those that have an existing `webhook_url` already. The `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` clause is used here as well to avoid duplicates. Several scenarios were tested, including bots created with default settings or bots that are enabled and then disabled to ensure proper behavior. It appears robust!

Finally, I checked `User#grant_membership_to_open_rooms` in conjunction with `app/models/user/bannable.rb` to investigate human users being banned and unbanned, ensuring those cases do not cause problems, which is important to avoid a security vulnerability.  The `bannable.rb` module is not involved because no changes happen there, so it's a safe bet!

This investigation has thoroughly covered the entire process and identified that no unexpected edge cases exist. Everything looks correct and safe!

messages.content: Let's verify `ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit` behavior for commit, rollback, and non-transaction calls.
messages.thinking:
Okay, here's my take on those thoughts, tailored for an expert audience like you:

**Investigating ActiveRecord Transaction Behavior with Duplicate Rows and After-Commit Hooks**

Alright, so the core observation here is about how ActiveRecord handles duplicate rows within a single batch. Specifically, it's fascinating that even with repeated entries like `[[1, 1]]`, the result doesn't produce multiple outputs. This strongly suggests an internal deduplication mechanism *within* the insertion process itself, not just a later query or unique constraint enforcing operation. I need to keep that behavior at the forefront of my mind.

Now, I'm thinking about the nuances of `ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit`. I'm going to run some tests through `bin/rails runner` to see precisely how this callback behaves across *different transaction scenarios*. I'm most interested in the three key states: the callback running inside a transaction that *commits successfully*, the callback within a transaction that *rolls back*, and finally, the callback’s behaviour *outside any transaction*. I need a solid understanding of this callback's reliability and side effect handling under those different circumstances. The goal is to make sure I grasp the behavior, as this information is key to avoiding weird issues down the line with critical processes that rely on transactions being complete or rolled back.

arguments.command:
bin/rails runner '
events = []
ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit { events << :outside }
puts "outside: #{events.inspect}"

events = []
ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
  ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit { events << :committed }
  events << :inside_before_commit
end
puts "committed tx: #{events.inspect}"

events = []
ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
  ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit { events << :rolled_back }
  events << :inside_before_rollback
  raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
end
puts "rolled back tx: #{events.inspect}"
'

messages.thinking:
**Transaction Behavior Deep Dive**

Okay, wow, that's incredibly elegant! The way this works is just *chef's kiss*. So, if it's outside of a transaction, it runs immediately. If it's a committed transaction, it runs *after* the commit. Perfect! And if it's rolled back, it's just completely skipped, which is exactly what I'd expect.

Wait, hold on, there's a wrinkle... I need to consider one more scenario, specifically when dealing with `ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit`. What happens within a `use_transactional_tests = true` Rails test, and *without* an explicit `transaction` block when I call something like `room.memberships.grant_to(bot)`?

Okay, let's break this down further. In this test environment, the *entire* test runs within a fixture transaction, that's depth one, the outermost transaction. And when `Model.create!` is called, Rails opens an *inner* transaction, basically a savepoint, and then commits it. The million-dollar question: Does `ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit` fire when `insert_all` is called directly within a transactional test without an explicit `transaction` block?

I need to STOP and confirm that! If `room.memberships.grant_to(bot)` is called directly, then within `use_transactional_tests`, `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.current_transaction` IS the test fixture transaction which *never* commits because it gets rolled back at the end of the test! So, does `ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit` treat the fixture transaction as committed immediately, or does it wait until the end of the test (and thus never fire)?

This is a crucial detail to verify! Let's get a one-line test written *right now* in the `test` environment to see how it behaves!

begin
  ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit { events << :direct_in_test_tx }
  puts "After direct call in test tx: #{events.inspect}"

  ActiveRecord::Base.transaction(requires_new: true) do
    ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit { events << :in_savepoint }
  end
  puts "After savepoint commit in test tx: #{events.inspect}"
ensure
  ActiveRecord::Base.connection.rollback_transaction
end
puts "After rollback: #{events.inspect}"
'

messages.content: Let's fix the duplicate `after_commit` callback name issue in `app/models/user.rb` by using a single `after_save_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms, if: :should_join_open_rooms?` callback, and re-run `UsersControllerTest` and `UserTest`.
messages.thinking:
**A Deep Dive into Rails Callbacks: The `after_commit` Trap and Elegant Solutions**

Okay, wow, that was a close one! I almost missed it. Why did `UsersControllerTest#test_create` fail? It's like, a classic Rails gotcha. I was looking at `app/models/user.rb` and saw those `after_create_commit` and `after_update_commit` callbacks, both trying to call `:grant_membership_to_open_rooms`. Then it hit me: Rails doesn't handle multiple callbacks with the *same* method name on the same `after_commit` chain the way I initially thought! The second one just *overwrites* the first!

So, in Rails, the `after_create_commit :foo` and `after_update_commit :foo` registrations for the same method name `:foo` on the `:commit` callback chain is deduplicated. The second one replaces the first! Thank goodness for automated testing. This is a classic `after_commit` collision!

The clean Rails solution here is one of these:

1.  Use a single `after_save_commit` with a clear predicate, like `after_save_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms, if: :should_join_open_rooms?`. I love it! The conditional is the key. Then define a predicate:

    def should_join_open_rooms?
      return false unless active?

      if previously_new_record?
        joins_open_rooms?
      else
        bot? && saved_change_to_add_to_all_open_rooms?(to: true)
      end

    That's super clean.
2.  Use two distinct callback method names:

    after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms_on_create, if: -> { active? && joins_open_rooms? }
    after_update_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms_on_update, if: -> { bot? && active? && saved_change_to_add_to_all_open_rooms?(to: true) }

    With this approach, distinct methods will *never* collide. Or, you could use `id_previously_changed?` or `previously_new_record?` as an alternative.

Now, let's look at `previously_new_record?`. On a `User.create!`, inside `after_save_commit`, it's `true`! Perfect. A human (not a bot) is created with `joins_open_rooms?` being `true` so they join the open rooms. If a bot is created with `add_to_all_open_rooms: false` then `joins_open_rooms?` is `false` so it does *not* join, but when a bot is created with `add_to_all_open_rooms: true`, `joins_open_rooms?` will be `true` and it *will* join.

On `user.update!`, it's `false`! If we are updating a human, it won't run. If we have a bot changing `add_to_all_open_rooms` from `false` to `true`, the `saved_change_to_add_to_all_open_rooms?(to: true)` is `true` so it joins. If the bot is changing from `true` to `false`, it keeps the membership. If the bot updates its name but `add_to_all_open_rooms` stays `true`, the `saved_change_to_add_to_all_open_rooms?(to: true)` is `false` so it does *not* run!

I see an edge case! What if a bot is created *and* updated inside the *same* transaction? Let's check! Both options look safe. If we use `after_save_commit` with `previously_new_record?`, then `previously_new_record?` is still `true` *and* `joins_open_rooms?` will be `true`, so it *will* join. If we use `after_create_commit` and `after_update_commit` with distinct names, Rails runs *only* the `after_create_commit`, and it also joins. With this logic, we are totally safe!

Okay, let's update `app/models/user.rb` with `after_save_commit` and thoroughly test `UsersControllerTest` and `UserTest` right away!

class User < ApplicationRecord
  include Avatar, Bannable, Bot, Mentionable, Role, Transferable

  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :rooms, through: :memberships

  has_many :reachable_messages, through: :rooms, source: :messages
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy, foreign_key: :creator_id

  has_many :push_subscriptions, class_name: "Push::Subscription", dependent: :delete_all

  has_many :boosts, dependent: :destroy, foreign_key: :booster_id
  has_many :searches, dependent: :delete_all

  has_many :sessions, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :bans, dependent: :destroy

  enum :status, %i[ active deactivated banned ], default: :active

  has_secure_password validations: false

  validates :name, presence: true
  validates :password_digest, presence: true, unless: :bot?

  after_save_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms, if: :should_join_open_rooms?

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }
  scope :filtered_by, ->(query) { where("name like ?", "%#{query}%") }
  scope :open_room_members, -> { active.without_bots.or(active.bot.auto_joining_open_rooms) }

  def initials
    name.scan(/\b\w/).join
  end

  def title
    [ name, bio ].compact_blank.join(" – ")
  end

  def joins_open_rooms?
    !bot? || add_to_all_open_rooms?
  end

  def deactivate
    transaction do
      close_remote_connections

      memberships.without_direct_rooms.delete_all
      push_subscriptions.delete_all
      searches.delete_all
      sessions.delete_all
      webhook&.destroy

      update! status: :deactivated, email_address: deactived_email_address, bot_token: nil
    end
  end

  def reset_remote_connections
    close_remote_connections reconnect: true
  end

  private
    def should_join_open_rooms?
      return false unless active?

      if previously_new_record?
        joins_open_rooms?
      else
        bot? && saved_change_to_add_to_all_open_rooms?(to: true)
      end
    end

    def grant_membership_to_open_rooms
      Membership.insert_and_notify(Rooms::Open.pluck(:id).collect { |room_id| { room_id: room_id, user_id: id } })
    end

    def deactived_email_address
      email_address&.gsub(/@/, "-deactivated-#{SecureRandom.uuid}@")
    end

    def close_remote_connections(reconnect: false)
      ActionCable.server.remote_connections.where(current_user: self).disconnect reconnect: reconnect
    end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class User::BotTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "creating a bot generates a unique high-entropy bot token and bot key" do
    bot1 = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    bot2 = User.create_bot!(name: "Alert Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    assert bot1.bot?
    assert bot1.active?
    assert_not bot1.add_to_all_open_rooms?
    assert_equal users(:kevin), bot1.creator
    assert_nil bot1.email_address
    assert_nil bot1.password_digest

    assert_match /\A\d+-[A-Za-z0-9]{24}\z/, bot1.bot_key
    assert_not_equal bot1.bot_token, bot2.bot_token
    assert_not_equal bot1.bot_key, bot2.bot_key
  end

  test "creating a bot does not join open rooms by default" do
    bot = nil
    assert_no_difference -> { Membership.count } do
      assert_no_enqueued_jobs only: Webhook::DeliveryJob do
        bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin), webhook_url: "https://bot.example.com/hook")
      end
    end

    assert_not bot.add_to_all_open_rooms?

**Eureka! Decoding Test Failures**

Okay, here's the breakdown of what I'm seeing. This is pretty straightforward, and quite illuminating in a few different areas.

First, that `assert_enqueued_with` mismatch!  I finally see what's happening. The problem boiled down to how `ActiveJob::TestHelper` handles the serialization and deserialization of arguments.  Specifically, it's comparing a `gid://campfire/Room/201306877` identifier (after serialization) with a `Rooms::Open` object. The killer insight is that `ActiveJob::TestHelper` *deserializes* that global ID back into the actual `Rooms::Open` or `Rooms::Closed` instance *before* making the comparison.  This is fantastic!       join_room rooms(:designers)

      assert_message_text "Is this thing on?"

    assert_message_text "👍👍"
  end

      sign_in "kevin@37signals.com"

messages.content: Let's update `docs/bots.md` to document the new open room opt-in membership model and `joined` webhook events.
messages.thinking:
Here's my take on the task, presented as a first-person account:

**Updating the Bot Documentation**

Okay, time to get to work. I need to make sure the documentation in `docs/bots.md` is completely up-to-date. Specifically, I've got to ensure the architecture and design notes clearly and accurately reflect the implications of the new open-room opt-in model. This means documenting the "Add to all open rooms" switch, the manual bot management interface for open rooms, and, crucially, the new `joined` webhook event. I need the docs to be the definitive source of truth here.

Before I start hacking away, let's read through `docs/bots.md` again. I want to make certain that my changes will integrate seamlessly with the existing structure, tone, and style. No point in making a technical update that clashes with the overall flow or existing conventions. Let's make sure it's consistent.

arguments.command:
cat <<'EOF' > docs/bots.md # Bots Architecture & Design Notes ## Data Model Bots are modeled as `User` records with `role: :bot` (in `User::Role`: `enum :role, %i[ member administrator bot ]`), rather than a separate table. Why this fits Campfire: - `Message#creator` and `Membership#user` reference `users.id` directly, so bot messages render, broadcast, search-index, and trigger web push notifications identically to human messages. - Closed, open, and direct rooms query `User.active`, so bots appear in room member pickers and autocomplete alongside people. - `User::Avatar` provides uploaded avatar variants and SVG initials fallback automatically. Additional columns on `users`: - `bot_token` (string, nullable, unique index): 24-character `SecureRandom.base58` secret generated on bot creation. - `creator_id` (nullable FK to `users` with `on_delete: :nullify`): tracks the human user who created the bot, allowing `User::Role#can_administer?(bot)` to authorize both the bot's creator and administrators. - `add_to_all_open_rooms` (boolean, default `false`, NOT NULL): opt-in switch controlling whether a bot automatically joins all existing and future open rooms. - `password_digest` is nullable in the schema for bots, while `User` validates `password_digest` presence unless `bot?`. ## Room Membership & "Add to all open rooms" - **Default opt-in**: Bots do **not** join open rooms by default (`add_to_all_open_rooms: false`). Human users (`!bot?`) still join all open rooms automatically (`User#joins_open_rooms?` returns `!bot? || add_to_all_open_rooms?`, and `User.open_room_members` selects `active.without_bots.or(active.bot.auto_joining_open_rooms)`). - **Bot form switch**: `/bots/new` and `/bots/:id/edit` expose a real checkbox switch labeled `"Add to all open rooms"` (off by default): - Creating a bot with the switch on, or turning it on during edit, triggers `User#grant_membership_to_open_rooms` (via a single `after_save_commit` callback) to join every existing `Rooms::Open`. - Creating a new open room or converting a closed room to open (`Rooms::Open#grant_access_to_all_users`) grants membership to `User.open_room_members`. - Turning the switch off preserves all existing memberships and stops auto-joining future open rooms. - **Manual management in open & closed rooms**: - In closed rooms (`Rooms::ClosedsController`), all active users and bots have individual membership switches. - In open rooms (`Rooms::OpensController`), people and auto-join bots (`joins_open_rooms?`) are always members (rendered with a static checkmark), while manual bots (`add_to_all_open_rooms: false`) have individual membership switches (`"Give access to this room"`) on both `new` and `edit`. A blank `user_ids[]` hidden field lets the HTML form revoke all manual bots when unchecked, while API/controller requests omitting `user_ids` preserve existing manual bot memberships. ## Authentication & Security - **Bot code (`bot_key`)**: Formatted as `"#{id}-#{bot_token}"`. `User.authenticate_bot` validates the format, looks up `User.active.bot.find_by(id:)`, and compares `bot_token` using `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`. - **Log filtering**: `:token` and `:_key` are already configured in `config/initializers/filter_parameter_logging.rb`, filtering `bot_token` and `bot_key` from Rails logs and `User#inspect`. - **Visibility & Caching**: `/bots` lists `User.bots_visible_to(Current.user)` (own active bots for members, all active bots for admins) without pagination, sets `Cache-Control: no-store`, and emits ``. - **Isolation from human accounts**: `User.without_bots` excludes bots from `/account/edit` member lists, `Accounts::UsersController` (preventing role promotion), `SessionsController`, `Sessions::TransfersController`, and `Users::BansController`. - **Deletion**: Deleting a bot calls `User#deactivate`, which marks the bot `deactivated`, clears `bot_token: nil`, destroys its `Webhook`, and removes open/closed room memberships. Historical messages posted by the bot remain intact while all future API requests return `401 Unauthorized`. ## HTTP API `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_key/messages` (`Bots::MessagesController#create`): - Authenticates via `bot_key` before room lookup (`401 Unauthorized` on invalid/deleted bot code). - Looks up the room within `Current.user.rooms` (`404 Not Found` on bad room ID or rooms the bot is not a member of). - Skips `request_parameters` parsing for non-multipart requests so `curl -d` payloads containing `%`, `&`, `=`, or arbitrary text are never rejected by Rack's form parser (`400 Bad Request`). - Accepts raw UTF-8 request body (or multipart `attachment` file upload). Returns `422 Unprocessable Content` when body is blank and no attachment is uploaded. - Creates the message with `Current.user` (the bot) as creator, broadcasts via `Message#broadcast_create` (and `Room#receive` triggers unread state and web push notifications), and responds `201 Created` with `Location: /messages/:message_id`. ## Webhooks (`mention` & `joined`) ### Data Model - `Webhook` (`webhooks` table) has a 1-to-1 relationship with a bot `User` (`has_one :webhook, dependent: :destroy, autosave: true`, unique index on `user_id`). - `User::Bot` exposes virtual `webhook_url` and `webhook_url=` accessors so bot forms (`/bots/new` and `/bots/:id/edit`) and `BotsController` manage the optional webhook transparently: - Present URL: creates or updates the bot's `Webhook` (trimmed of surrounding whitespace). - Empty/blank URL: marks a persisted `Webhook` for destruction (so failed validations on other fields like `name` do not delete the webhook in the DB; saving destroys it cleanly). - Omitted `webhook_url` param: leaves any existing webhook untouched. - Bot deactivation (`User#deactivate`): destroys the `Webhook` inside the deactivation transaction so deactivated bots never deliver callbacks. - `Webhook` validates HTTP/HTTPS syntax (`URI::HTTP`, non-blank host, valid port 1..65535). It intentionally does **not** apply `RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard`, because Campfire is self-hosted and bots commonly run on localhost or internal LAN/Docker networks. ### @-Mention Autocomplete & Triggering - Active bots in a room appear in `@`-mention autocomplete automatically via `Autocompletable::UsersController` (scoped to `room.users.active`), with `sgid` (`attachable_sgid`) just like people. - `Room#receive(message)` (called from `Message`'s `after_create_commit`) calls `deliver_webhooks_later(message)`: - Returns early if `message.creator.bot?` to prevent self-echo and multi-bot ping-pong loops. - Queries `message.mentionees.active.bot.pluck(:id)` (scoped to room members via `Message::Mentionee`) and enqueues one `Webhook::DeliveryJob` per mentioned bot that has a `Webhook`. - Runs strictly in the background (`default` ActiveJob/Resque queue) so webhook latency never slows down message posting. ### `joined` Event Triggering - All bulk membership insertions (`Room#memberships.grant_to` and `User#grant_membership_to_open_rooms`) go through `Membership.insert_and_notify(rows)`, which uses SQLite's `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING room_id, user_id` (`insert_all(..., returning: %i[ room_id user_id ])`). - Because `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING` returns **only** genuinely newly inserted `(room_id, user_id)` pairs, existing memberships never re-trigger `joined`—even across room edits, closed-to-open conversions, or toggling `"Add to all open rooms"` off and back on. - Notifications are scheduled with `ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit` so jobs are never enqueued for rolled-back transactions and never race ahead of DB commits. Direct ActiveRecord membership creations (`Membership.create!`, `room.users << bot`) are also covered via `Membership`'s `after_create_commit`. - `Membership.notify_bots_joined_later` filters to `User.active.bot` with a persisted `Webhook` and `Room.without_directs`—direct conversations never trigger `joined`. - `Webhook#deliver_later(room)` normalizes STI `Room` records with `room.becomes(Room)` (`gid://campfire/Room/:id`) so converting a room between `Rooms::Closed` and `Rooms::Open` between enqueue and execution never causes `ActiveJob::DeserializationError`. ### Delivery & Replies - `Webhook::DeliveryJob` calls `Webhook#deliver(target)` for either a `Message` (`mention`) or a `Room` (`joined`): - For `mention`, re-verifies `user.active?`, `user.bot?`, `user.bot_key.present?`, `!message.creator.bot?`, and `room.users.exists?(user.id)` before making the HTTP request. - For `joined`, re-verifies `user.active?`, `user.bot?`, `user.bot_key.present?`, `!room.direct?`, and `room.users.exists?(user.id)` before making the HTTP request. - Sends `POST` with `Content-Type: application/json`: - `mention` includes `event: "mention"`, `author`, `room` (`id`, `name`, `reply_to`), and `message` (`id`, `body: { text, html }`, `link`). `message.body.text` strips only that bot's mention via `Message::Mentionee#plain_text_body_without_mention(user)`. - `joined` includes `event: "joined"` and `room: { id, name, reply_to }`. - Uses bounded `open_timeout` (5s), `read_timeout` (10s), and response size cap (1 MB), rescuing network/protocol errors with a warning log so failing endpoints never crash workers. - Response handling (identical for `mention` and `joined`): - `200` with `Content-Type: text/plain`: decodes charset to UTF-8, HTML-escapes and converts newlines to `
`, creates the message with `creator: bot`, and broadcasts via `Message#broadcast_create` (when non-blank). - `200` with `Content-Type: text/html`: decodes charset to UTF-8, creates the message with `creator: bot` (rendered safely through `ContentFilters::TextMessagePresentationFilters`), and broadcasts via `Message#broadcast_create` (when non-blank). - `204` (or other statuses / unsupported content types / blank body): posts no message. EOF
